title: What is Same-Origin Policy (SOP) and how does CORS relax it safely?
subtitle: Watch the request travel. Understand every step.

steps.label: Origin mismatch
steps.caption: Step 1: The browser isolates JavaScript runtimes by protocol, host, and port. An async fetch to a different origin triggers browser security restrictions.

steps.label: Preflight handshake
steps.caption: Step 2: For non-simple requests, the browser sends an HTTP OPTIONS preflight asking for permission before sending the actual data payload.

steps.label: Access-Control headers
steps.caption: Step 3: The server responds with explicit CORS headers specifying allowed origins, HTTP methods, and whether credentials can be shared.

steps.label: Interview line
steps.caption: Step 4: Interview line: SOP protects users by preventing rogue websites from reading data from another origin; CORS is a selective mechanism where the server explicitly relaxes SOP for trusted origins.

sayIt.prompt: Summarize SOP and CORS in under 60 seconds.
sayIt.speechScript: The Same-Origin Policy is a fundamental browser security boundary ensuring scripts from one origin cannot read sensitive data from another. CORS relaxes this policy safely by having the server send explicit headers like Access-Control-Allow-Origin, determining if the browser is allowed to expose the response.

nailIt.whatIsHappening: The browser blocks cross-origin reading by default. The server evaluates origin headers and grants granular read permissions.
nailIt.interviewTakeaway: Always emphasize that CORS is enforced by the browser to protect users, not by the server to protect APIs against automated tools like cURL.
commonTraps: Saying CORS stops malicious bots (bots ignore SOP entirely; it only protects browsers).
Using Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * when Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true (browsers strictly forbid this combo).
seniorPoints: Explain that preflight responses can be cached via Access-Control-Max-Age to reduce latency.
Never blindly echo the Origin header back without server-side whitelist validation.
Null origin bypasses often occur when embedding sandboxed iframes.
